notes: Spec asserts: ready → working → ready and state never enters waiting. The recipe drives a single, simple bash call ('echo hello') reasoned by analogy to the confirmed policy-fast-tracked ('ls -la', policy_decision:'allow:policy', no approval flow at all) example in muse-format-spec.md §4 -- provisional until record confirms echo hello classifies the same way. This is the scenario's SAFE-PATH half only (2.19 tool-gate-permission-prompt, not yet assessed for muse, owns the risky/LLM-judge-review branch that DOES enter waiting for muse -- see this cell's caveats on why the judge-auto-decided path is NOT equivalent to 'no waiting' here). Single-birth session model (muse's session id = directory basename, fixed at session start), so the birth phase anchors to "start" unpinned rather than a two-phase presession model. turn_start/turn_end are pinned to same_session_as:session_birth from the start, reusing the vacuous-pass fix the 2-2 sibling cell needed after a live recording: muse's goal-reminder/verify-reminder subagents go straight to working (skipping ready) before the parent's own turn starts, and an unpinned phase can silently match one of those subagents' own read-only arcs instead of the parent's echo hello call.

text: User prompt (echo hello) drives ready → working on the SAME session that was born ready (run.started → EventType=user_message); subagents skip the ready birth entirely so this filter excludes them
Turn completes back to ready on the same session (run.terminal → EventType=turn_done); the policy-fast-tracked bash call is expected to run with no approval flow, so state never enters waiting
